title: Feedback conduit — synthesis and prioritized probe sprint notes
body:
Purpose
This note compiles recent customer feedback (May–Jun 2026), clusters it into actionable problem buckets, and proposes a 2-week probe sprint (low-risk fixes + 1 medium experiment) to reduce customer pain and gather signal for product work. Aim: move from reactive patches -> validated small changes that reduce inbound tickets by ~20% for the targeted cohorts.

Background and scope
- Sources: CS triage threads, Postman logs of high-latency calls, three enterprise onboarding interviews (RetailCorp, FinData, HealthForge), and runtime ops incidents from May–Jun 2026.
- Focused on inference runtime / hosted API pain that maps to product or infra changes (not UX copy or docs only).
- We intentionally excluded long-term feature asks that need >3 sprints. Those are captured in product backlog with ticket prefix CS-BACKLOG.

Representative customer quotes (anonymized)
- "We get occasional 400s when we switch model variants in our fallback policy — hard to recover." — Retail product lead
- "Embedding calls spike costs when we batch on the client; need better default batching guidance." — ML platform engineer at FinData
- "Can we pin quantization profiles? We had a regression after auto-quantize and it cost us dev cycles." — HealthForge infra owner

Cluster map (5 buckets)
1) Fallback variant transition instability
   - Symptoms: 400/5xx after automatic route/fallback switch, cache misses, KV rewarm latency.
   - Signal: 12 tickets May–Jun (enterprise tier), 3 P0 incidents (short outages), correlated with rollout windows.

2) Embedding batching and client-side misconfiguration
   - Symptoms: customers batching too aggressively leading to token-cost spikes, timeouts in mobile clients.
   - Signal: billing anomalies in 7 customers, 2 refund requests, one churn risk.

3) Auto-quantize / transparent profile regression risk
   - Symptoms: model outputs changed for tight QA prompts after auto-quantize enabled.
   - Signal: 4 escalations, ask for explicit pinning controls.

4) Observability blind spots for per-route latency and token breakdowns
   - Symptoms: customers can't map API latency regressions to model/kernel changes.
   - Signal: repeated ask to expose per-route percentiles and token-level cost traces.

5) Documentation and onboard checklists are fragmented
   - Symptoms: new customers miss config flags (cache TTL, prefix caching) that materially affect latency.

Quick fixes (2-week probe sprint)
- Quickfix A (1 day): Add a soft-warning hook in the console for routes with high fallback-rate. Show recent fallback % in last 24h. Product + Console dev. Expected signal: immediate reduction in confusion tickets.
- Quickfix B (3 days): Runtime: introduce a 100–300ms graceful KV-rewarm path for fallback variant switch (serve stale KV while rewarming). Engineering effort: infra + serving-runtime (small kernel path). Risk: low. Metric: 95th p95 latency during variant switch.
- Quickfix C (2 days): Add 'recommended batching' snippet into SDKs (py/js) and server-side advisor that surfaces when customers send >X tokens/request. Owners: DX + SDK.
- Quickfix D (2 days): Add a 'pin quantize profile' toggle in the model config (console + API). This prevents auto-switches during rollouts. Owners: product + model-onboarding team.

Medium experiment (2-week)
- Experiment E: Controlled rollout of variant-switch circuit breaker. When a fallback is detected, hold new traffic on previous variant for 30s while warming compatible KV shards; if errors persist, auto-fallback to a safe variant and create a diagnostic bundle for CS.
  - Hypothesis: reduces P0 incidents related to variant rollout by 60%.
  - Success criteria: fewer P0s across 30 days post rollout for pilot accounts; mean time to recover (MTTR) reduced by >40%.
  - To run: pick 5 pilot customers (one per region, mix of enterprise & scale).

Impact estimate (business/ops)
- Low effort quickfixes estimated to reduce incoming CS tickets in the bucket by ~20–30% in 30 days.
- Medium experiment requires ~3 engineer-weeks (runtime + infra + observability) and will need an infra owner on call during rollout. If successful, we estimate savings of 0.5–1 FTE CS time per month across enterprise accounts.

Acceptance criteria for probe sprint items
- Quickfixes: deployed to staging and validated with synthetic traffic; owners confirm telemetry and example diagnostic bundles exist.
- Medium experiment: documented rollback plan, observability dashboards for pilot, and a pre-commit checklist for on-call.

Risks and open questions
- Risk: graceful-serve of stale KV could slightly reduce quality for a small subset of requests. Tradeoff needs to be communicated in release notes and customer pilot invitations.
- Open Q1: What SLA changes (if any) do we need to make to enable circuit breaker tweaks for enterprise? Legal and SRE input required.
- Open Q2: Do we expose 'pin quantize' only in console or also allow API flag for infra-as-code customers? (Owner: product decision)

Operational runbook sketch (for experiment)
- Pre-rollout: run compatibility check on model shard mapping; notify pilot customers 72h in advance.
- Rollout window: low traffic window for each region; infra on-call and runtime lead present.
- Post-rollout: automated health-check aggregation for 24h; if fallback rate >5% sustained, revert.

Proposed tickets (starter templates)
- jira:CS-3241 — quickfix-console-fallback-widget (owner: Liam Chen)
- jira:CS-3242 — runtime-kv-graceful-warm-path (owner: Ravi Narang)
- jira:CS-3243 — sdk-batching-snippet-and-advisor (owner: Sofia Martinez)
- jira:CS-3244 — model-config-pin-quantize (owner: product)
- jira:CS-3245 — experiment-variant-circuit-breaker-pilot (owner: Devon Brooks)

Action items (next 7 days)
- [ ] Align owners and confirm sprint allocation (Aisha) — by 2026-07-08
- [ ] Post quickfix console widget design in #cs-console for 24h review (Liam) — by 2026-07-07
- [ ] Create telemetry events (fallback_rate, kv_rewarm_time, batch_token_warning) and add to infra ETL (Ravi) — by 2026-07-09
- [ ] Draft pilot invite for 5 customers and run legal check on opt-in (Devon + Legal) — by 2026-07-10

Notes to reviewers
- Prioritize low-risk, high-observable wins first. If product wants to deprioritize 'pin quantize' we should still land SDK advisor and KV warm path (largest immediate reduction in tickets).
- Expect some early customer pushback about serving slightly stale KV during fallback; prepare a short FAQ and an opt-out mechanism for quality-sensitive customers.

Appendix: quick logs and examples (anonymized)
- Example error pattern: POST /v1/generate 500 -> logs show 'kv-miss after switch' -> spike in p95 to +350ms for 3–9s window.
- Billing spike example: single embedding job where client batched 2000 short texts into 1 call, token-units billed at 3x expected due to per-text overhead.

If this plan looks good we can finalize tickets and schedule the probe sprint to start 2026-07-13.

Document owner: Aisha Patel (CS)
